summary:
TerraRotate AI is a farmer-led prototype for exploring climate-aware crop rotation. It brings together farmer-provided field details, NASA climate data, and NASA Earth observation imagery so users can compare rotation options with their evidence and assumptions visible. Its tools also support water-budget planning, sourced vegetation analysis, historical climate comparisons, and farmer feedback.

The project addresses the Field Shift challenge by making climate and Earth observation resources easier to explore in the context of farm decisions. It distinguishes numeric data from visual map layers, reports missing information, and explains the limits of each analysis. Its rotation rankings are transparent, rule-based comparisons, not yield predictions or prescriptions.

This matters because climate information is most useful when people can understand where it comes from and what it can—and cannot—say about their fields. TerraRotate AI offers an inspectable starting point for discussion between farmers and local experts, while highlighting where local data and validation are still needed.

GitHub repository: (https://github.com/UzaibBashir/TerraRotate_AI)
details:
Project details

TerraRotate AI is a farmer-led web prototype for exploring crop-rotation choices alongside climate and Earth observation context. Farmers can enter a location, current crop, water availability, priorities, and optional soil details. The app retrieves gridded climate information from NASA POWER and displays NASA GIBS imagery, including MODIS, VIIRS, GPM IMERG, and SMAP layers. It compares three rotation options with an explainable, weighted rule-based method.

Applications and functions

TerraRotate AI can support early-season planning and conversations between farmers and local agricultural experts. Its functions include:

  • Comparing crop-rotation sequences based on selected priorities.
  • Viewing NASA climate information and regional satellite imagery.
  • Exploring water-budget scenarios based on farmer-entered assumptions.
  • Summarizing sourced vegetation observations supplied by the user.
  • Comparing historical climate patterns at selected locations.
  • Grouping user-supplied sample points and recording farmer feedback.
  • Saving field details in the browser and printing a field report.

How it addresses the problem

Climate and Earth observation data can be difficult to connect to practical farm decisions. TerraRotate AI brings selected data and farmer-provided context into one interactive workflow. It shows sources, assumptions, and missing information so users can inspect how an option was ranked and identify what needs local checking. This can make climate information easier to discuss and use when considering rotation choices under changing weather and water conditions.

What makes it distinct

The prototype combines farmer-led inputs, NASA data, and transparent rotation comparisons while distinguishing numeric data from visual imagery. Satellite browse maps provide regional visual context; their colors are not treated as field measurements. The rankings are exploratory comparisons, not prescriptions or yield forecasts.

Comparison with traditional approaches

Farm planning often relies on experience, local advice, records, and information gathered from separate sources. Those approaches provide essential local knowledge, but comparing climate context and rotation options can take time and may make assumptions difficult to track. TerraRotate AI organizes selected evidence and makes its comparison rules visible. It is intended to support farmer judgment and expert advice, not replace them.

Example use case

A farmer with limited irrigation enters their field location, current crop, and main priorities. TerraRotate AI displays available NASA POWER climate context and NASA GIBS imagery, then compares three rotation ideas using its visible scoring rules. The farmer reviews the assumptions and data gaps and uses the options as a starting point for discussion with a local agricultural advisor.

Prototype readiness

TerraRotate AI is a working exploratory prototype with NASA data connections and browser-local field saving. It has not been validated through field trials or agronomic review. Its broad crop profiles and ranking rules need local adaptation, and its results should be checked against field conditions and expert guidance before informing decisions.

Limitations

The prototype’s broad crop profiles and rotation rules need regional agronomic review and field validation. Gridded climate data and satellite imagery may not represent conditions within a specific field. Some analysis tools require users to provide sourced measurements; sample values are illustrative or synthetic and should not be interpreted as farm observations. The app does not diagnose crop health or predict yield. Optional Supabase feedback sync requires configuration; browser-local storage is the default.

Technology and repository

The frontend uses Next.js, React, and JavaScript. The backend uses Python and Flask, with NASA POWER and NASA GIBS services. No special hardware is required.

GitHub repository: TerraRotate_AI
dataRefs: NASA POWER daily temperature and precipitation, daily water cycle context, and historical monthly climate profiles
NASA POWER Projection API climate scenario data (SSP1‑2.6, SSP2‑4.5, SSP3‑7.0). The interface supports comparison, though the tested Kashmir location returned no usable projection values.

NASA Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS) map imagery and layer legends:- MODIS Terra and Aqua true-color imagery - VIIRS SNPP true-color imagery - MODIS Terra and SNPP VIIRS 8-day NDVI imagery - GPM IMERG precipitation imagery - SMAP L4 soil-moisture imagery
NASA Earthdata Login for authenticated access to selected archived product downloads. Those archives are not currently integrated into the application.
